Yes
From the QA lens, committing the real-shape corpus before the red enables rigorous red-first testing: each shape family provides concrete inputs and expected outputs that the red commits directly as executable test rows. This guarantees that tests fail red before implementation and prevents passing malformed or unhandled states. Pre-measuring reference behavior across diverse real shapes catches regressions early and avoids repeated fix rounds.
